request.title: The L volume of Britannica
request.prompt: Painterly dark-fantasy illustration in the style of a cinematic tabletop RPG book spread: wide 16:9 landscape composition, dramatic lighting with warm ember-orange highlights against cold ice-blue shadows, rich texture, a clear focal point. No text, no captions, no speech bubbles, no logos, no watermark. Scene: inside a dim, lamplit passenger carriage of a train stopped dead in a dark mountain tunnel, frost on the windows. Ulrick: a broad-shouldered human paladin with short swept-back dark brown hair and a full dark beard, wearing heavy dark plate armour with bronze-orange pauldrons and a long white cloth tabard over the armour. He sits on a bench with his sleeve rolled up, a fresh bite mark on his forearm bandaged in cloth, insisting with a stoic face that he is absolutely fine. Beside him, Lyrial: a lean half-elf bard with long brown hair worn in loose braids and beaded locks, green eyes and light stubble, in a worn brown leather coat over an olive jacket and white shirt; he has pulled an enormous, dusty, ancient encyclopedia out of his bag and is flipping through it with a frown of deep concentration, reading the one article that might help. The book is obviously centuries out of date and is the only volume he owns: the only lettering in the whole image is a single large letter L embossed in gold on its spine. Warm lamp glow against the cold blue dark of the tunnel. Understated comedy.
